correctness.rationale: The norm ||x||_r=max(||x||∞,r|lim x|) is an absolute lattice norm for r>=1. For any increasing positive directed family in its unit ball with supremum f in c, coordinatewise 0<=f<=1 implies ||f||_r<=r, while finite-one vectors u^k↑1 have norm1 and supnorm r in the renorming, proving exact demicontinuity r. c* decomposes as a coordinate l1 functional plus alpha*lim; tails v^k=1-u^k decrease to 0, so order continuity forces alpha=0. Conversely l1 coefficients define order-continuous functionals; finite-support sign tests recover exact dual norm ||a||1, hence dual norming gauge ||x||∞ and sharp r ratio at 1. Coordinatewise finite truncations squeeze Lorentz norm of bounded x between ||x||∞ from both sides; unbounded sequences cannot have finite Lorentz gauge. For every norm-one Hahn–Banach L extending ordinary limit, L1=1 and ||L||=1 force positivity on [0,1], so max{sup,r|Lx|} is a lattice norm extending the c family. Truncations show sharp demicontinuity r there too. All arguments symbolic, including r=1.
